title: Why was the U.S. interstate highway system built?
sources: Federal Highway Administration Interstate System History

lines.text: Why did President Eisenhower spend hundreds of billions of dollars constructing forty-eight thousand miles of interstate highways?
It wasn't just to make cross-country road trips scenic and convenient for families.
In nineteen nineteen, a young officer named Dwight Eisenhower crossed America with a military convoy, taking sixty-two grueling days over dirt tracks.
lines.caps: Young Eisenhower *took | 62 grueling days to cross *America

lines.text: During World War Two, he witnessed the sheer logistical speed of the German Autobahn.
lines.caps: Saw how Germany's *Autobahn | moved troops at lightning *speed

lines.text: In nineteen fifty-six, he signed the National Defense Highway Act to evacuate cities during nuclear attacks and move tanks nationwide in days.
lines.caps: Built to evacuate *cities | and move military *tanks rapidly!

lines.text: Overpasses were built with sixteen-foot clearances specifically to accommodate intercontinental ballistic missile convoys.
lines.caps: Overpasses were *measured | to fit military *missile carriers!

lines.text: The interstate highway system remains the largest public works project in American history.
